clue.text: Another sad loser's case just the job for the assessor

indicators.note: another version of the words that follow suggests they are to be recast in a new order
read as a state of affairs or condition the letters are put into, a second hint that they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: A gloomy claimant's file is exactly the sort of work an insurance assessor deals with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' and 'case' both signal the anagram of SAD LOSER plus JUST; the possessive 's adds nothing. 'the job for the' is padding linking to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurer sends this professional to value the damage claimed, so the role is a kind of claims assessor.

clue.text: Chemical produced by cow, fish and insect

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal, cow or bull
id is a variant spelling of ide, a freshwater carp-family fish
an ant is a common insect

explanation.surface: A substance seems to be made from a farm animal, a fish and a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: ID is the rarer spelling of IDE, a European fish, given in Chambers; it saves a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxidizing agent is a reactive substance studied in chemistry, so it is a chemical.

clue.text: Take a look round most editions of the paper

indicators.note: one word set round another means it surrounds the second

parts.note: to scan is to take a quick look

indicators.note: editions are different versions, so the word most appears in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Glance over most issues of the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'editions' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal on 'most'. The paper is the Edinburgh daily, and a SCOTSMAN also reads it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scotsman is a long-running Scottish daily newspaper.

clue.text: Fight over outstanding student

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: a debt outstanding is one still due
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A scrap over a brilliant pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' reads as excellent but means owed; L for learner is the British L-plate on a new driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel is a formal combat between two people, a kind of fight.

clue.text: Less of a tender place for attributions

definitions.meaning: to bid a lower price, putting in a smaller tender
read playfully as below a quotation, where the source of a quote is credited

explanation.surface: A lower bid and where the credits go.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: a quote's attribution is printed beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Underquoting means offering a lower price than rivals; split, it describes the spot below a quotation where credit appears.

clue.text: Sat back to note the flavour

indicators.note: back tells us the word sat is read in reverse

parts.note: te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone sat back to record a flavour in a tasting notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal of 'Sat'; TE is the seventh note of the do-re-mi scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste and flavour are synonyms for the sensation food gives the palate.

clue.text: Nastier sort of wine

indicators.note: sort of hints at a loose version of the word, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rather more unpleasant kind of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' signals the anagram of NASTIER; fittingly, many find the resinated wine an acquired taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: A switch in power for the couch potato

definitions.text: A switch in power for the couch potato

parts.words: A switch in power for the couch potato
parts.note: the switch lets a lazy viewer change channels from the sofa, holding the power to the set in one hand, not a shift in political power

explanation.surface: A political change of power suits a lazy sofa-dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: A handset that switches television channels from a distance is exactly what a sofa-bound viewer relies on.

clue.text: Odds on finishing German banker's riotous expenditure

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds at the start of a race
finishing means ending
a banker is a river, having banks; the Spree flows through Berlin

explanation.surface: Bets placed on a German banker's wild spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is a crossword joke for a river; the Spree runs through Berlin. SP is the betting term for starting price.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild bout of buying, a spree of spending, is lavish uncontrolled expenditure.

clue.text: Typical example of English poem composed about it

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the following word
a poem composed is put together, so its letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A quintessential English poem written on the subject of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' signals the anagram, and 'about' puts the rearranged poem round IT, all after E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect instance that embodies a type, a typical example.

clue.text: Spoke about including data transmission initially on the computer

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters are mixed
initially picks the opening letters of the words data and transmission

explanation.surface: Someone talked about including data transmission at first on a PC.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' adds D and T, first letters by 'initially', to SPOKE; 'about' scrambles the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Desktop describes something on a computer screen, as in a desktop icon or desktop machine.

clue.text: Hit back on the old stones

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
back means the word for hit is reversed

parts.note: to slap is to hit

explanation.surface: A blow struck back at the elderly with rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' signals the reversal of the word for hit; 'on' places it after O in an across clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Opals are iridescent gemstones.

clue.text: It describes well! the exchange rates to a reader of 3 down

indicators.note: exchange suggests letters swapping places, so the word rates is rearranged

parts.note: a reader of a Scottish paper is a Scot, typified by the name Ian

explanation.surface: A pun on currency exchange rates sent to a Scottish newspaper reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' turns RATES into ARTES; IAN is a typical Scot reading the Scotsman (3 down). The definition's exclamation mark flags 'well' as a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Artesian is the adjective for a well where pressure forces water up without pumping.

clue.text: A good looking Italian can be poison

definitions.meaning: in Italian the two words mean beautiful lady
deadly nightshade, a toxic plant and drug

explanation.surface: A handsome Italian can prove deadly.
explanation.walkthrough: The '4' is a scanning stray; the clue starts at 'A'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade gets its Italian name, meaning fair lady, from its use to dilate women's pupils; the plant is highly toxic.

clue.text: More commonsense about the first edition is not essential

parts.note: extra means more, additional

indicators.note: about means the word for common sense goes round the following letter

parts.note: nous is British slang for practical good sense

indicators.note: the first picks the opening letter of edition

explanation.surface: A newspaper's first edition shows extra sense, but it is unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: NOUS goes 'about' E, the first of 'edition', making NEOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extraneous is irrelevant or superfluous, not needed.

clue.text: Cover up for Indian terrorists' second comeback

indicators.note: a comeback is a return, so the pieces before it are read in reverse

parts.note: the IRA, the Irish Republican Army

explanation.surface: A cover-up for an Indian terrorist group's renewed attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comeback' reverses IRA plus S together.
explanation.definitionFit: A sari is the draped garment worn by many Indian women, a covering.

clue.text: Saviour without a horse set in most untidy fashion

indicators.note: without means letters are taken away from the word before

parts.note: the Messiah is the saviour
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape, so the word set is reshaped

explanation.surface: A messiah without a horse sat in a very untidy way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is slang for heroin, abbreviated H. 'fashion' turns SET into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Messiest is the superlative of messy, meaning the least tidy.

clue.text: Office of president?

parts.note: the question mark hints at a shape: the US president's office in the White House is named for its form

explanation.surface: Is this where the president works?
explanation.definitionFit: The Oval Office is the elliptical room of the US president, so the shape names his office.

clue.text: It brings up supplies

parts.note: a delivery by aircraft carries stores up into the sky, not a supply line reaching a front

explanation.surface: Something that hauls up provisions.
explanation.definitionFit: An airlift is the transport of goods by aircraft, flying in supplies.

clue.text: Clogging up, say, in embrace

indicators.note: in places the word for say inside the word for embrace

parts.note: to cling is to hold tight, embrace
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Getting choked, so to speak, in a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' reads as 'for example' but means UTTER, which goes 'in' CLING.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluttering is filling a space with mess, clogging it up.

clue.text: One girl placed it back in the old century — how stupid!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name

indicators.note: in means the reversed word goes inside the following letters
back tells us the word it is reversed

explanation.surface: A girl placed it back in the last century, which was foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' makes TI, placed 'in' O and C (old, century).
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'how stupid' expresses that something is foolish or senseless.

clue.text: Variations on the dry melody

indicators.note: musical variations rework a theme, so these words are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Musical variations on a dry tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Variations' signals the anagram of ON THE DRY; it borrows a music word for a music answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A threnody is a lament, a mournful song or ode for the dead, so it is a melody.

clue.text: Sound of final operation on the French river

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second
final picks the closing letter of operation

parts.note: the Oise is a river in northern France

explanation.surface: The report of a last military operation on a river in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' takes the last letter of 'operation'; the Oise joins the Seine near Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise is any audible sound.

clue.text: On board, politician will try to make economies

indicators.note: one piece placed on another follows it in an across clue

parts.note: a ski is a long narrow board for gliding on snow
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Once on the board, a politician will try to cut costs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' reads as joining a committee, but MP goes 'On' SKI.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to stint or economise, using too little of something.

clue.text: Pretty little elm, perhaps, to one who lisps

indicators.note: a speaker who cannot say R properly turns the word into a W sound

parts.note: an elm is an example of a tree

explanation.surface: A dainty little elm as described by a lisping speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Strictly R said as W is not a lisp, but the clue uses 'lisps' loosely for babyish speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or dainty, prettily small.

clue.text: Love to nail the charge from one point of view

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
a pin is a slender fastener like a nail
an ion is an atom with an electric charge

explanation.surface: Love leads to nailing the accusation, from one standpoint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' reads as an accusation but is an electrically charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a personal view or belief, one point of view among others.

clue.text: Fight the others left within borders of Worcestershire

indicators.note: within places the pieces inside the outer letters
borders of picks the first and last letters of Worcestershire

parts.note: the rest are the others

explanation.surface: Battle the remaining forces left inside Worcestershire's borders.
explanation.walkthrough: W and E, the first and last letters of Worcestershire (an English county), go round REST and L.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrestle is to grapple, a form of fighting.

clue.text: Treatment of disease with catheter is up to doctor

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Treating illness with catheters is a matter for the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to doctor' signals the anagram of CATHETER IS UP; the printed text's extra S would give one letter too many.
explanation.definitionFit: Therapeutics is the branch of medicine concerned with treating illness.
